question: What is disease notification primarily defined as?

options.A: Conducting laboratory research on new pathogens
options.B: Official reporting of specific diseases to health authorities
options.C: Vaccinating rural communities against common infections
options.D: Treating patients in a specialized isolation ward

explanation: Disease notification specifically refers to sharing case data with public health agencies for tracking and control. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h1)

question: Why is timely disease notification vital for a country's healthcare system?

options.A: It prevents localized outbreaks from turning into widespread epidemics
options.B: It guarantees immediate financial compensation for affected hospitals
options.C: It eliminates all forms of infectious diseases in rural areas
options.D: It replaces the need for routine childhood immunization programs

explanation: Early reporting allows public health teams to contain infections before they spread across communities. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h1)

question: A primary objective of public health surveillance is to...

options.A: Detect sudden changes in disease frequency
options.C: Provide personal insurance for health workers

explanation: Surveillance tracks disease patterns to spot unusual increases or outbreaks early. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h2)

question: How do nurses directly support public health surveillance objectives?

options.A: Managing financial budgets for state health ministries
options.B: Documenting clinical findings accurately and submitting records
options.C: Designing national health policies in legislative meetings
options.D: Purchasing medical equipment for primary health centers

explanation: Accurate nursing documentation forms the foundation of reliable public health data. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h2)

question: Which disease requires immediate reporting within 24 hours in Nigeria?
explanation: Lassa fever is a high-consequence viral hemorrhagic disease that demands immediate emergency notification. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h3)

question: Why are notifiable diseases separated into immediate, weekly, and monthly categories?

options.A: To limit public panic about common community illnesses
options.B: To ensure laboratories only test samples on specific days
options.C: To reduce the total amount of paperwork nurses must complete
options.D: To match the reporting speed with the epidemic threat level

explanation: Categorization ensures dangerous outbreaks receive instant attention while routine trends are tracked steadily. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h3)

question: Who is the first designated health officer to receive case reports from a primary clinic?

options.B: Local Government Area Disease Surveillance Officer
options.D: Minister of Health at the federal capital

explanation: The LGA surveillance officer acts as the primary link between frontline clinics and higher health authorities. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary function of the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control in the reporting chain?

options.A: Dispensing monthly salaries to all rural nurses
options.B: Building new residential quarters for health staff
options.C: Managing federal responses and national coordination
options.D: Treating individual patients in primary clinics

explanation: The NCDC serves as the national apex body coordinating disease prevention and emergency response. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h4)

question: What does IDSR stand for in Nigerian public health practice?
explanation: IDSR is the regional framework used to harmonize surveillance activities across health facilities. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why is using a standardized line list important during disease notification?

options.A: It replaces the need for any verbal communication
options.B: It automatically cures the infectious condition being reported
options.C: It organizes patient details uniformly for easy tracking
options.D: It guarantees free medical treatment for every patient listed

explanation: Uniform line lists prevent missing information and allow epidemiologists to analyze outbreak trends clearly. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h5)

question: An active case search during an outbreak investigation involves what action?

options.A: Checking financial receipts for medical supply purchases
options.B: Finding hidden cases in the community that have not visited a clinic
options.C: Searching hospital pharmacy shelves for expired medications
options.D: Reviewing staff attendance registers at primary health centers

explanation: Active case finding ensures individuals who stay home or use alternative care are identified and managed. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h6)

question: A nurse assisting an outbreak investigation team is most likely asked to...

options.A: Negotiate international funding for epidemic control
options.B: Prescribe emergency antibiotics without medical supervision
options.C: Construct isolation wards in rural settlements
options.D: Gather exposure histories and interview affected families

explanation: Nurses use clinical interviewing skills to trace contacts and determine infection sources during outbreaks. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why are community health nurses uniquely positioned for early disease detection?

options.A: They possess exclusive authority to run national public health labs
options.B: They control the distribution of national health budgets
options.C: They are the only healthcare workers trained in Nigeria
options.D: They maintain daily contact with local families and community groups

explanation: Frequent grassroots interaction allows nurses to notice unusual health changes before they reach hospitals. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a core notification duty of a community health nurse?

options.A: Passing national health laws in the legislative assembly
options.B: Ensuring prompt dispatch of forms to the LGA office
options.C: Educating local leaders about reporting dangerous symptoms
options.D: Maintaining a high index of suspicion for unusual illnesses

explanation: Legislation is the function of lawmakers, whereas nurses focus on clinical identification, education, and reporting. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h7)

question: How does patient stigmatization negatively impact disease notification systems?

options.A: It prevents nurses from writing accurate clinical notes
options.B: It delays the delivery of international monetary grants
options.C: It drives infected individuals away from clinics, leading to unreported cases
options.D: It increases the cost of purchasing laboratory reagent kits

explanation: Fear of social rejection causes people to hide illnesses, resulting in missed diagnoses and hidden outbreaks. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h8)

question: A practical solution to improve data transmission from remote health facilities is...

options.A: Restricting reporting duties to federal capital hospitals
options.B: Closing down rural clinics during disease outbreaks
options.C: Integrating digital mobile tools for reporting
options.D: Stopping all community outreach programs entirely

explanation: Mobile health technology helps bypass paper delays and improves communication between remote posts and central authorities. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T4#GNS313_U4_T4_h8)
